title: Felix and the Parish
premise: Sebastian Quintana, a retired detective turned failing bookshop owner, is hired by a nervous young woman named Ada to prove that her grandfather's death thirty years ago was not the accident the parish claims — because if it wasn't murder then, it will be murder again soon, when the last witness dies. As Sebastian pulls at alibis woven across three decades, she discovers the parish council buried a drowning in the tidal marshes and has been paying silence ever since. When Ada herself becomes the next target, Sebastian must choose between protecting her found family of parish regulars and exposing the truth. In the end, the tide gives up what it took — the grandfather's watch, and with it proof — and the parish's quiet conspiracy collapses, though justice arrives outside any courtroom.
about_author: K. M. Okafor is a former court clerk who spent fifteen years transcribing other people's confessions before writing her own mysteries. She lives in a coastal town where the fog keeps its secrets, much like her characters do.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A rain-soaked stranger, Ada Okonkwo, walks into Quintana's Books and pays triple rate for an impossible job: prove a murder hasn't happened yet. Sebastian, prideful and broke, accepts despite every instinct. The emotional beat is wary curiosity — the thrill of a case stirring a woman who thought she'd retired from caring.

chapters.title: The Alibi of Thirty Years
chapters.summary: Alternating Sebastian and Ada POVs. Digging into the 1995 drowning of Ada's grandfather, Sebastian finds five parish elders whose stories align too perfectly, rehearsed like scripture. Ada reveals her grandmother's dying letter hinting at blackmail. The beat deepens: loyalty to the parish versus the truth Ada needs, as Sebastian realizes the whole town may be complicit.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. After Sebastian confronts the eldest councilman, Ada's cottage is ransacked and she vanishes; the marsh tide is rising toward the spot where the grandfather drowned. Racing the water, Sebastian searches the flats and finds the old watch wedged in the silt — engraved with a date that breaks the official timeline. The beat is terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Verdict Without a Court
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, closing with Sebastian's. Rescued but defiant, Ada chooses truth over safety: she reads her grandmother's letter aloud at the parish meeting as Sebastian lays the watch on the table. The conspirators fracture, one confesses, and the town must live with what it buried. The beat is bittersweet catharsis — justice outside the law, and two lonely people becoming family.
